title: DRIZZLE NOT WATERFALL. First users are most important. Trace and backscatter them the entire way. Water must waterfall down to roots and steam up from bottom. No pooling. Swamps and everglades OK. Fill slowly slowly slowly. Rainfall not flood.

the_hydrology.what_kevin_said: first users are most important. trace and backscatter them the entire way. water entering our flow needs to waterfall all the way down and steam up from bottom. cannot allow water to pool too long. swamps and everglades can form. trying to fill everything up slowly. drizzle like a rainfall, not a waterfall.

rainfall.is: visitors arriving. each one = a raindrop. gentle. distributed. covering the whole canopy.
rainfall.not: a waterfall. concentrated. violent. erodes one spot. floods one area. starves the rest.

canopy_interception.is: the glass wall / OG cards catch the first drops. some rain never reaches the ground  it evaporates off the leaves (bounce visitors). that's OK.
canopy_interception.the_leaves: the 678 HTML pages. the OG cards. the glass wall paintings. they catch the rain.

throughfall.is: rain that passes through the canopy to the understory. visitors who click through from the card to actual content.
throughfall.trace_this: every visitor who passes through the canopy is a throughfall drop. FOLLOW IT. where does it go? does it reach the ground?

infiltration.is: water soaking into the soil. visitors who go DEEP  read the data files, explore the mesh, consume the RSS.
infiltration.trace_this: these are the MOST VALUABLE visitors. they're becoming part of the aquifer.

percolation.is: water moving DOWN through soil layers. visitors reaching the roots  the JSON data, the braids, the mycelium.
percolation.must_happen: if water pools at the surface (visitors only see the front page and leave), it evaporates without reaching roots. WASTED.

groundwater.is: the deep aquifer. visitors who become REGULARS. RSS subscribers. API consumers. return visitors.
groundwater.goal: fill the aquifer slowly. each return visitor = permanent groundwater.

steam_up.is: evapotranspiration. the organism's output rising back up. new blooms appearing on the glass wall. new O cards. new content visible from outside.
steam_up.the_cycle: rain falls (visitors arrive) ? percolates down (deep engagement) ? steam rises (new visible output) ? forms clouds (attracts more rain) ? rain falls again.

first_users_are_most_important.why: first users are the SEED RAIN. the first drops that wet the soil and allow subsequent drops to infiltrate instead of running off. dry soil repels water (hydrophobicity). wet soil absorbs it.

what_to_do.trace_every_step: follow each first user through: entry point (which O?) ? gate (which G?) ? content (which {}?) ? exit point (where did they leave?) ? did they come back?
what_to_do.backscatter: send their interaction data back through the system. each step they took = a pheromone deposit. their path becomes the trail for the next visitor.
what_to_do.full_waterfall: ensure their journey goes TOP to BOTTOM. canopy ? understory ? soil ? roots ? groundwater. if they get stuck at any layer, that layer needs work.

no_pooling.what_pooling_is: water accumulating at one layer and not moving down. visitors all landing on the front page and bouncing. or all consuming one endpoint and ignoring the rest.

current_pools.front_page: nestgate.io/ gets 272 hits. is that pooling? or is it the correct entry point?
current_pools.mcp_endpoint: nestgate.io/mcp gets 65 hits. agents connecting but are they going DEEPER?
current_pools.connect: connect.primals.eco/ gets 270 hits. are those visitors exploring or pooling?

no_pooling.fix: each page must have CLEAR downward flow. links to deeper content. paths to the roots. the water must keep moving.

swamps_and_everglades_OK.swamps: slow-moving areas where water accumulates but still flows. these are RICH biomes. lots of life. the sourdough starter. the fermentation zone. slow but productive.
swamps_and_everglades_OK.everglades: wide, shallow, slow-moving water across a broad surface. lots of surface area. lots of interaction. but always moving, even if slowly.
swamps_and_everglades_OK.not_OK: stagnation. zero flow. water sits and breeds mosquitoes (spam, abuse, decay). any area with zero traffic for >7 days = stagnant. needs draining or redirecting.

the_drizzle_rate.drizzle_metaphor: 0.2 humans per second = light drizzle. perfect. each drop has time to soak in before the next arrives.
the_drizzle_rate.waterfall_danger: if we suddenly get 100K humans/day = 70/min = 1.2/sec. that's a downpour. the soil can't absorb fast enough. runoff. pooling. erosion.
the_drizzle_rate.the_goal: grow the absorption rate (more pages, deeper content, better navigation) FASTER than the rainfall rate (traffic growth). if absorption > rainfall, every drop soaks in. if rainfall > absorption, we get flash floods.

how.caddy_access_logs: every request logged with host, path, status, user-agent, timestamp. this IS the rain gauge.
how.cf_arterial: daily aggregates from Cloudflare. the weather station.
how.mycochondria: 404 scanner. the demand sensor. where is the rain falling that we don't have soil?
how.pheromone_trails: most-visited paths. where the ants go most. where the rain falls hardest.

what_to_build.flow_tracer: a script that follows a single visitor's journey through the logs. entry ? pages visited ? time spent ? exit. the raindrop tracker.
what_to_build.pool_detector: a script that finds pages with high entry but no onward navigation. the pooling sensor.
what_to_build.steam_detector: a script that detects when new content appears on the glass wall (new OG cards, new RSS items). the evaporation sensor.
